# ADS-5261 — Support Keyword Facets from Autocomplete Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make the plugin honour `products.filter.<field>=<value>` query parameters, so search URLs generated by Nosto's autocomplete keyword facets actually filter the result set.

**Architecture:** Nosto's search-js serialises filters into query params keyed by the **Nosto field path** (`products.filter.skus.customFields.größe`), while `FilterHandler` only recognises params keyed by **Nosto facet id**. We add a dedicated parser that decodes the search-js URL contract into a value/range filter, and a normalisation step in `FilterHandler` that runs *before* the existing id-based lookup. Where the field maps to a known facet id we rewrite to the canonical id so the existing sidebar and filter-removal logic keeps working unchanged; otherwise we apply the filter directly to the `SearchOperation`.

**Tech Stack:** PHP 8.1+, Shopware 6, PHPUnit 11.5, `nosto/php-sdk` 7.7.4.

---

## Background: the verified URL contract

Decoded from the deployed search-js bundle (`d21m4dsqdd3b9h.cloudfront.net/<merchant>/search/templates/main/deployment/<ts>/bundle.js`) and confirmed live on matratzen-concord.de. **Do not guess at this format — it is not Shopware's convention.**

| Aspect | Contract | Contrast with existing plugin code |
|---|---|---|
| Key prefix | `products.filter.` | facet id (24-hex), no prefix |
| Nested field | dot-joined: `skus.customFields.größe` | n/a |
| Literal `.` inside a segment | escaped as `::` | n/a |
| Multiple values | joined by `\|\|` | `FILTER_DELIMITER = '\|'` (single pipe) |
| Range | `gte~lte` single param | `min-<id>` / `max-<id>` param pair |
| Exclusive bounds | `[gt~` and `~lt]` | n/a |
| Multiple ranges | comma-separated | n/a |
| Literal `~` in a value | escaped as `%7E` | n/a |
| Legacy range separator | `-+` also accepted on decode | n/a |

Evidence of the bug (live, matratzen-concord.de):

| URL | Results |
|---|---|
| `?search=viscoschaum` | 19 |
| `?search=viscoschaum&68836248ec4277760d058e18=140x200cm` (facet id) | 9 |
| `?search=viscoschaum&products.filter.skus.customFields.größe=140x200cm` (field path) | **19 — silently ignored** |

That merchant works around it with a hand-maintained per-domain `serpUrlMapping` in their template bundle. This plan removes the need for that.

**Local repro (already set up):** `enableSearch` is now `true` for sales channel `019C4C81EF3A711D924B1D3C65DD2809`; `nostoCookieFilter*` cookies confirm the Nosto path is live, not the Shopware fallback.

| URL on `https://vladimir.chagorovski.shopware67.com:8000` | Now | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| `/search?search=main` | 3 | 3 |
| `/search?search=main&products.filter.brand=Shopware+Fashion` | **3 (bug)** | **1** |

`brand` is filterable in Nosto with no facet configuration, which is why it is the integration probe. (Verified directly against the Nosto API: `brand=Shopware Fashion` narrows `main` from 3 → 1.)

## AMENDMENT (2026-08-10, after Task 2-5 code review) — read this before Task 6

Code review of the parser surfaced a defect that invalidates the original Task 6 approach. **PHP rewrites `.` to `_` in query-parameter names** (`parse_str`/`$_GET`), so `$request->query->all()` never contains a `products.filter.*` key. Verified against this repo's vendored Symfony:

```
Request::create('/search?search=main&products.filter.brand=X')->query->all()
  => ['search' => 'main', 'products_filter_brand' => 'X']
```

Consequence: the original Task 6, which loops over `$request->query->all()`, would pass its unit tests (they supply hand-written keys with real dots) and **silently do nothing on a live storefront**. The raw query string must be used instead — `$request->server->get('QUERY_STRING')` preserves both the dots and the percent-encoding.

### What Nosto actually puts on the wire

Confirmed by replicating search-js's encoder (`Eo()` escapes a literal `~` to the *text* `%7E`, then `URLSearchParams` percent-encodes):

| Case | On the wire | After ONE urldecode |
|---|---|---|
| literal `~` in a value | `A%257EB` (double-encoded) | `A%7EB` → parser's `ESCAPED_TILDE` → `A~B` |
| multi-value | `Blue%7C%7CRed` | `Blue\|\|Red` |
| range separator | `10%7E20` | `10~20` |
| nested UTF-8 field | `...customFields.gr%C3%B6%C3%9Fe` | `...customFields.größe` |
| the `.` separators | **not encoded** | unchanged |

So the existing `ESCAPED_TILDE` handling in the parser is **correct and load-bearing** — a literal tilde survives as `%7E` after one decode precisely because Nosto double-encodes it. Do not "simplify" it away. Decoding must be exactly one `urldecode` per name and per value; decoding twice would turn a literal tilde into a range separator.

End-to-end proof of the corrected path (all four parse correctly, `A~B` stays a value):

```
products.filter.brand                     field=brand                   values=["A~B"]
products.filter.colour                    field=colour                  values=["Blue","Red"]
products.filter.price                     field=price                   ranges=[{"gte":"10","lte":"20"}]
products.filter.skus.customFields.größe   field=skus.customFields.größe values=["140x200cm"]
```

### Task 5b (new, do before Task 6) — query-string extraction + range-bound validation

See the task section added after Task 5 below.

### Task 6 has been rewritten in place

The Task 6 section below has been updated to use `parseQueryString()`. Its tests now drive a real `Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request` rather than hand-written parameter keys, so this class of bug cannot pass unit tests again.

## Scope

**In scope:** decoding `products.filter.*` params into value and range filters; applying them on both the initial-request and cookie-based request paths; keeping the sidebar's selected/removal behaviour intact.

**Search and category pages both, for free.** `SearchRequestHandler` and `NavigationRequestHandler` share one `FilterHandler` instance constructed in `AbstractRequestHandler::__construct()` (`src/Search/Request/Handler/AbstractRequestHandler.php:36`) and both reach it through `configureSearchOperation()` (`:203`). Fixing `FilterHandler` therefore covers category listings as well as search, with no extra wiring. Autocomplete only lands on `/search`, but Nosto SERP/category links use the same serialisation.

**Out of scope (deliberate):**
- Changing Nosto's autocomplete or template bundle. This is a server-side fix only.
- `gte`/`lte` inclusive range bounds. `SearchOperation::addRangeFilter()` in `nosto/php-sdk` 7.7.4 emits only `gt`/`lt` (`vendor/nosto/php-sdk/src/Operation/Search/SearchOperation.php:209-231`), and `$filters` is `private`, so inclusive bounds cannot be expressed without an SDK change. The Nosto GraphQL API *does* accept `gte`/`lte` (`InputSearchRangeFilter`). The existing range-slider path has the same limitation, so this is consistent with current behaviour, not a regression. **Follow-up ticket needed against `nosto/php-sdk`.**

## Task 1: `NostoFieldFilter` value object

**Files:**
- Create: `src/Search/Request/Handler/NostoFieldFilter.php`

- [ ] **Step 1: Create the value object**

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Nosto\NostoIntegration\Search\Request\Handler;

/**
 * A single filter decoded from a `products.filter.<field>` query parameter.
 *
 * Either $values is non-empty (a terms filter) or $ranges is non-empty (a stats filter),
 * never both. Each range is a map with any of the keys 'gt', 'gte', 'lt', 'lte'.
 */
final class NostoFieldFilter
{
    /**
     * @param string[] $values
     * @param array<int, array<string, string>> $ranges
     */
    public function __construct(
        public readonly string $field,
        public readonly array $values = [],
        public readonly array $ranges = [],
    ) {
    }

    public function isRange(): bool
    {
        return $this->ranges !== [];
    }
}
```

Create `src/Search/Request/Handler/NostoFieldFilterParser.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Nosto\NostoIntegration\Search\Request\Handler;

/**
 * Decodes Nosto search-js filter query parameters into NostoFieldFilter objects.
 *
 * Nosto's autocomplete and SERP links serialise filters keyed by the Nosto field path
 * rather than by facet id, e.g.:
 *
 *     ?products.filter.skus.customFields.größe=100x200cm
 *
 * This class is intentionally dependency-free so the (fiddly) format rules are covered
 * by plain unit tests. See docs/superpowers/plans for the full decoded contract.
 */
class NostoFieldFilterParser
{
    public const FIELD_PREFIX = 'products.filter.';

    public static function supports(string $key): bool
    {
        return str_starts_with($key, self::FIELD_PREFIX);
    }

    public function parse(string $key, string $rawValue): ?NostoFieldFilter
    {
        if (!self::supports($key)) {
            return null;
        }

        $field = mb_substr($key, mb_strlen(self::FIELD_PREFIX));
        if ($field === '' || $rawValue === '') {
            return null;
        }

        return new NostoFieldFilter($field, [$rawValue]);
    }
}
```

```php
    /**
     * Nosto joins multiple values for one field with '||' and escapes any literal '~'
     * (its range separator) as '%7E'.
     *
     * @return string[]
     */
    protected function parseValues(string $rawValue): array
    {
        $values = [];

        foreach (explode(self::VALUE_DELIMITER, $rawValue) as $value) {
            $value = str_replace(self::ESCAPED_TILDE, '~', $value);
            if ($value !== '') {
                $values[] = $value;
            }
        }

        return $values;
    }
```


Add these methods to the class:

```php
    /**
     * Nosto serialises a range as '<lower><separator><upper>', with square brackets marking
     * an exclusive bound: '[10~20]' means gt=10, lt=20 while '10~20' means gte=10, lte=20.
     * Multiple ranges for one field are comma-separated. A literal '~' inside a value is
     * escaped as '%7E', so an unescaped separator is what distinguishes a range from a value.
     *
     * @return array<int, array<string, string>>
     */
    protected function parseRanges(string $rawValue): array
    {
        $separator = match (true) {
            str_contains($rawValue, self::LEGACY_RANGE_SEPARATOR) => self::LEGACY_RANGE_SEPARATOR,
            str_contains($rawValue, self::RANGE_SEPARATOR) => self::RANGE_SEPARATOR,
            default => null,
        };

        if ($separator === null) {
            return [];
        }

        $ranges = [];

        foreach (explode(self::RANGE_DELIMITER, $rawValue) as $rawRange) {
            $range = $this->parseRange($rawRange, $separator);
            if ($range !== []) {
                $ranges[] = $range;
            }
        }

        return $ranges;
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function parseRange(string $rawRange, string $separator): array
    {
        if (!str_contains($rawRange, $separator)) {
            return [];
        }

        [$lower, $upper] = array_pad(explode($separator, $rawRange, 2), 2, '');

        $range = [];

        $lowerIsExclusive = str_contains($lower, '[');
        $lower = $this->cleanBound($lower);
        if ($lower !== '') {
            $range[$lowerIsExclusive ? 'gt' : 'gte'] = $lower;
        }

        $upperIsExclusive = str_contains($upper, ']');
        $upper = $this->cleanBound($upper);
        if ($upper !== '') {
            $range[$upperIsExclusive ? 'lt' : 'lte'] = $upper;
        }

        return $range;
    }

    protected function cleanBound(string $bound): string
    {
        return str_replace(
            self::ESCAPED_TILDE,
            '~',
            preg_replace('/[\[{\]}\']/', '', $bound) ?? '',
        );
    }
```

**Files:**

## Task 5b: Query-string extraction and range-bound validation

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/Search/Request/Handler/NostoFieldFilterParser.php`
- Modify: `tests/Unit/Search/Request/Handler/NostoFieldFilterParserTest.php`

Two changes: a `parseQueryString()` entry point that reads the raw query string (fixing the Critical defect above), and `is_numeric` validation of range bounds so malformed input degrades to the value path instead of shipping garbage to the Nosto API.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Append inside `NostoFieldFilterParserTest`:

```php
    public function testParsesFieldPathFiltersFromRawQueryString(): void
    {
        // Exactly what Nosto's search-js puts on the wire: dots unencoded, '||' as %7C%7C,
        // range separator as %7E, and a literal tilde double-encoded as %257E.
        $queryString = 'search=main'
            . '&products.filter.brand=A%257EB'
            . '&products.filter.colour=Blue%7C%7CRed'
            . '&products.filter.price=10%7E20'
            . '&products.filter.skus.customFields.gr%C3%B6%C3%9Fe=140x200cm';

        $filters = (new NostoFieldFilterParser())->parseQueryString($queryString);

        self::assertCount(4, $filters);

        self::assertSame('brand', $filters[0]->field);
        self::assertSame(['A~B'], $filters[0]->values);
        self::assertFalse($filters[0]->isRange());

        self::assertSame('colour', $filters[1]->field);
        self::assertSame(['Blue', 'Red'], $filters[1]->values);

        self::assertSame('price', $filters[2]->field);
        self::assertSame([['gte' => '10', 'lte' => '20']], $filters[2]->ranges);

        self::assertSame('skus.customFields.größe', $filters[3]->field);
        self::assertSame(['140x200cm'], $filters[3]->values);
    }

    public function testParseQueryStringIgnoresNonNostoParameters(): void
    {
        $filters = (new NostoFieldFilterParser())->parseQueryString('search=main&sort=name-asc&p=2');

        self::assertSame([], $filters);

    {
        $parser = new NostoFieldFilterParser();

        self::assertSame([], $parser->parseQueryString(null));

    {
        $parser = new NostoFieldFilterParser();

        // A value delimiter inside what looks like a range means it is not a range.
        $filter = $parser->parse('products.filter.brand', '10~20||30');
        self::assertNotNull($filter);
        self::assertFalse($filter->isRange());
        self::assertSame(['10~20', '30'], $filter->values);

        // Non-numeric bounds are not a range either.
        $filter = $parser->parse('products.filter.brand', 'abc~def');
        self::assertNotNull($filter);
        self::assertFalse($filter->isRange());
        self::assertSame(['abc~def'], $filter->values);

    {

        self::assertNotNull($filter);
        self::assertTrue($filter->isRange());
        self::assertSame([['gte' => '10', 'lte' => '20']], $filter->ranges);
    }

    {
        // A bracket in the middle of a bound is not an exclusivity marker; the bound is
        // then non-numeric, so this is a value rather than a range.
        $filter = (new NostoFieldFilterParser())->parse('products.filter.price', '1[0~20');

        self::assertNotNull($filter);
        self::assertFalse($filter->isRange());
```

Add the constant below `SEGMENT_DOT_ESCAPE`:

```php
    /**
     * PHP rewrites '.' to '_' in query-parameter names, so the same parameter also appears
     * in $request->query under this mangled prefix. Callers use this to discard it.
     */
    public const MANGLED_FIELD_PREFIX = 'products_filter_';
```

Add the new entry point (place it directly above `parse()`):

```php
    /**
     * Decodes every Nosto field-path filter out of a raw query string.
     *
     * This MUST be given the raw query string (Symfony: $request->server->get('QUERY_STRING')),
     * not $request->query. PHP rewrites '.' to '_' in parameter names, so a parameter named
     * 'products.filter.brand' is only ever visible as 'products_filter_brand' in the parsed
     * bag and could never be recognised.
     *
     * Exactly one urldecode is applied per name and per value. That is deliberate: Nosto
     * escapes a literal '~' in a value to the text '%7E' before percent-encoding, so it
     * arrives here double-encoded and must still be '%7E' when parseValues() runs. Decoding
     * twice would turn a literal tilde into a range separator.
     *
     * @return NostoFieldFilter[]
     */
    public function parseQueryString(?string $queryString): array
    {
        if ($queryString === null || $queryString === '') {
            return [];
        }

        $filters = [];

        foreach (explode('&', $queryString) as $pair) {
            if ($pair === '' || !str_contains($pair, '=')) {
                continue;
            }

            [$name, $value] = explode('=', $pair, 2);

            $name = urldecode($name);
            if (!self::supports($name)) {
                continue;
            }

            $filter = $this->parse($name, urldecode($value));
            if ($filter !== null) {
                $filters[] = $filter;
            }
        }

        return $filters;
    }
```

Now tighten range parsing. Replace `parseRange()` and `cleanBound()` entirely with:

```php
    /**
     * A range bound is always numeric in this format. Anything else means the parameter is
     * not really a range (e.g. 'abc~def', or '10~20||30' where a value delimiter leaks in),
     * and the caller falls back to treating it as a value. That keeps malformed, user-supplied
     * URLs from sending nonsense bounds to the Nosto API.
     *
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function parseRange(string $rawRange, string $separator): array
    {
        if (!str_contains($rawRange, $separator)) {
            return [];
        }

        [$lower, $upper] = explode($separator, $rawRange, 2);

        $lowerIsExclusive = str_starts_with(trim($lower), '[');
        $upperIsExclusive = str_ends_with(trim($upper), ']');

        $lower = $this->cleanBound($lower);
        $upper = $this->cleanBound($upper);

        // Both bounds empty is not a range; a present-but-non-numeric bound invalidates it.
        if ($lower === '' && $upper === '') {
            return [];
        }
        if (($lower !== '' && !is_numeric($lower)) || ($upper !== '' && !is_numeric($upper))) {
            return [];
        }

        $range = [];

        if ($lower !== '') {
            $range[$lowerIsExclusive ? 'gt' : 'gte'] = $lower;
        }
        if ($upper !== '') {
            $range[$upperIsExclusive ? 'lt' : 'lte'] = $upper;
        }

        return $range;
    }

    protected function cleanBound(string $bound): string
    {
        return trim($bound, "[{]}' \t\n\r\0\x0B");
    }
```

Finally, `parseRanges()` must treat a partially-invalid set as "not a range at all", so the whole parameter degrades to a value. Replace its loop body handling:

```php
        $ranges = [];

        foreach (explode(self::RANGE_DELIMITER, $rawValue) as $rawRange) {
            if ($rawRange === '') {
                continue; // an empty segment carries no information
            }

            $range = $this->parseRange($rawRange, $separator);
            if ($range === []) {
                // A non-empty unparseable segment means this is not a range parameter.
                return [];
            }

            $ranges[] = $range;
        }

        return $ranges;
```

Two notes on `cleanBound()`:
- It strips brackets from the **edges only**, via `trim`'s character list — not everywhere. A mid-string bracket (`1[0`) must stay put so the bound reads as non-numeric and the parameter degrades to a value. Using `str_replace` would turn `1[0` into the numeric `10` and wrongly accept `1[0~20` as a range, contradicting `testDetectsExclusiveBoundsOnlyAtTheEdges`.
- It no longer un-escapes `%7E`: a numeric bound can never contain a tilde, and the `is_numeric` guard would reject it anyway.

An empty segment must be skipped rather than rejected. `10~20,` (a trailing comma is the classic survivor of a
hand-edited or truncated URL) would otherwise degrade into a terms filter on the literal string `"10~20,"`,
which matches no facet value — the shopper gets an empty result page instead of the range they asked for.
Non-empty garbage (`10~20,abc~def`) must still invalidate the whole parameter.

## Task 6: Apply parsed filters in `FilterHandler`

**Files:**
- Create: `tests/Unit/Search/Request/Handler/FilterHandlerTest.php`
- Modify: `src/Search/Request/Handler/FilterHandler.php`

This is the wiring. `handleFilters()` currently loops over `$request->query->all()` and resolves each key as a facet id. We add a separate pass that reads the **raw query string** for `products.filter.*` filters, and we drop the PHP-mangled `products_filter_*` keys from the id-based set so they cannot be mistaken for facet ids.

Two SDK constraints shape `applyFieldFilter()`:
- `SearchOperation::addValueFilter($field, $value)` appends one value per call and accumulates per field, so multi-value filters are applied in a loop.
- `SearchOperation::addRangeFilter($field, $min, $max)` emits only `gt`/`lt` and **merges into a single range per field**. Multiple comma-separated ranges therefore cannot be expressed; we apply the first and ignore the rest rather than merging them into a nonsense bound.

In `src/Search/Request/Handler/FilterHandler.php`, replace the body of `handleFilters()`:

```php
    public function handleFilters(
        Request $request,
        Criteria $criteria,
        SearchOperation $searchOperation,
        bool $newRequest = true,
    ): void {
        // Nosto's autocomplete and SERP links key filters by field path rather than facet id.
        // They must be read from the raw query string: PHP rewrites '.' to '_' in parameter
        // names, so they are not visible in $request->query at all. See ADS-5261.
        $this->applyFieldPathFilters($request, $searchOperation);

        $selectedFilters = $this->withoutFieldPathParameters($request->query->all());

        if (empty($selectedFilters)) {
            return;
        }

        if ($newRequest) {
            $this->handleNewRequest($selectedFilters, $criteria, $searchOperation);
        } else {
            $this->handleExistingRequest($selectedFilters, $request, $searchOperation);
        }
    }
```

Add these methods to the class:

```php
    private function applyFieldPathFilters(Request $request, SearchOperation $searchOperation): void
    {
        $queryString = $request->server->get('QUERY_STRING');

        foreach ($this->fieldFilterParser->parseQueryString(is_string($queryString) ? $queryString : null) as $filter) {
            $this->applyFieldFilter($filter, $searchOperation);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Drops the PHP-mangled counterparts of the field-path parameters (dots rewritten to
     * underscores) so the facet-id lookup never sees them.
     *
     * @param array<string, mixed> $selectedFilters
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    private function withoutFieldPathParameters(array $selectedFilters): array
    {
        $remaining = [];

        foreach ($selectedFilters as $filterId => $filterValues) {
            if (is_string($filterId) && str_starts_with($filterId, NostoFieldFilterParser::MANGLED_FIELD_PREFIX)) {
                continue;
            }

            $remaining[$filterId] = $filterValues;
        }

        return $remaining;
    }

    private function applyFieldFilter(NostoFieldFilter $filter, SearchOperation $searchOperation): void
    {
        if ($filter->isRange()) {
            // addRangeFilter() merges into one range per field, so only the first range is
            // representable. Applying the rest would corrupt the bounds.
            $range = $filter->ranges[0];

            $searchOperation->addRangeFilter(
                $filter->field,
                $range['gte'] ?? $range['gt'] ?? null,
                $range['lte'] ?? $range['lt'] ?? null,
            );

            return;
        }

        foreach ($filter->values as $value) {
            $searchOperation->addValueFilter($filter->field, $value);
        }
    }
```

```php
        private readonly FilterPayloadService $filterPayloadService,
    ) {
```

## Task 8: Sidebar selected-state and filter removal — ABANDONED, see finding below

> **OUTCOME (2026-08-10): implemented, then reverted. The approach cannot work.** Retained here because
> the finding is the useful part, and because it stops anyone re-attempting the same design.
>
> The plan assumed the storefront filter panel derives its selected state and removal links from the
> request query parameters, so rewriting a field path to its facet id on `$request->query` would make
> the existing machinery light up. That assumption is **false**, verified in the code:
>
> - `vendor/shopware/storefront/.../plugin/listing/listing.plugin.js:49` builds `_urlFilterParams` from
>   `window.location.search` — i.e. **client-side, from the browser URL**, fed to each filter plugin's
>   `setValuesFromUrl()` at `:115-116`.
> - `src/Resources/app/storefront/src/js/plugin/listing/filter-property-select.plugin.js:57-62` reads
>   `params[this.options.name]` (the facet id) split on `'|'`. The single-pipe delimiter choice was
>   right; the transport was not.
> - No template renders a `checked` attribute — zero hits across
>   `src/Resources/views/storefront/component/listing/`, and the core
>   `filter-multi-select-list-item.html.twig` has none either.
>
> `$request->query->set()` mutates only the in-process Symfony `Request`, which nothing in the render
> path or the JS ever reads. So the mechanism was inert.
>
> Worse than inert, in fact: `src/Search/Request/Handler/AbstractRequestHandler.php:307` iterates
> `$request->query->all()` and pushes **every** value as an `['ec', $value]` analytics event to Nosto's
> session-params endpoint. Injecting a synthetic facet-id parameter therefore leaked a bogus analytics
> event on every field-path search. That is why it was reverted rather than left in place as harmless
> dead code.
>
> **One real bug came out of it and was kept.** `withoutFieldPathParameters()` only strips the
> PHP-mangled `products_filter_*` keys, so an injected `facet-123` was *not* stripped and reached the
> id-based lookup — applying the same field twice (`value: ["Shopware Fashion","Shopware Fashion"]`)
> whenever the `nostoFilters` extension was populated, as it is on a live SERP. The plan's own test
> missed it by omitting that extension, which short-circuits the lookup. Fixed by snapshotting
> `$selectedFilters` before the field-path pass runs.
>
> **What would actually close the gap** (tracked as Follow-up 4, not implemented here): render the
> selection server-side from the `selected` flag Nosto already returns on each facet value
> (`src/Search/Response/GraphQL/Filter/Values/FilterValue.php:18`, populated at
> `Filter.php:85`, currently consumed by no template); or redirect field-path URLs to canonical
> `?<facet-id>=<value>` so the browser genuinely carries the parameter the JS looks for.

Why this task exists: after Task 6 the results are filtered, but Shopware's filter panel builds its checkbox names and "remove filter" links from the **facet id**. A filter that arrived as `products.filter.brand` has no facet id attached, so the shopper can see filtered results with nothing checked and no way to clear it. We fix that by rewriting the field path to its facet id whenever the current response knows one, and letting the existing machinery take over.

`IdToFieldMapping` maps facet id → field (`src/Struct/IdToFieldMapping.php`), so we need the reverse direction.

**Unverified assumption — check before trusting this task.** The approach assumes the storefront filter panel derives its selected state and removal links from the request query parameters. This could not be confirmed on the local store because the `shopware67` Nosto account currently has **zero facets configured**, so no sidebar renders at all. The unit tests below lock in the *mechanism* (field path → facet id rewrite), not the storefront rendering. Once a facet exists (see Follow-up 3), verify visually: apply `?search=main&products.filter.<field>=<value>`, confirm the checkbox shows as checked and that clicking the "×" clears it. If the panel turns out to read from the aggregation result rather than the request, the rewrite needs to move to `handleAvailableFilters()` instead — same reverse map, different injection point.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

In `FilterHandler::handleFilters()`, change the field-path call to pass the criteria:

```php
        $this->applyFieldPathFilters($request, $searchOperation, $criteria);
```

Replace `applyFieldPathFilters()` with:

```php
    private function applyFieldPathFilters(
        Request $request,
        SearchOperation $searchOperation,
        Criteria $criteria,
    ): void {
        $queryString = $request->server->get('QUERY_STRING');
        $fieldToId = $this->buildFieldToIdMap($criteria);

        $filters = $this->fieldFilterParser->parseQueryString(
            is_string($queryString) ? $queryString : null,
        );

        foreach ($filters as $filter) {
            $this->applyFieldFilter($filter, $searchOperation);
            $this->exposeUnderCanonicalId($filter, $request, $fieldToId);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Exposes a field-path filter under its facet id as well, so the storefront filter panel
     * renders it as selected and its removal link works. The filter is already applied to the
     * search operation by the caller, and the id-based lookup never sees these parameters
     * (they are stripped by withoutFieldPathParameters()), so this cannot double-apply.
     *
     * Range filters are skipped: the panel expresses those as separate `min-`/`max-` prefixed
     * parameters, which is a different convention from a value list.
     *
     * @param array<string, string> $fieldToId
     */
    private function exposeUnderCanonicalId(
        NostoFieldFilter $filter,
        Request $request,
        array $fieldToId,
    ): void {
        if ($filter->isRange()) {
            return;
        }

        $canonicalId = $fieldToId[$filter->field] ?? null;
        if ($canonicalId === null || $request->query->has($canonicalId)) {
            return;
        }

        // The panel joins multiple values with a single pipe, not Nosto's double pipe.
        $request->query->set($canonicalId, implode(self::FILTER_DELIMITER, $filter->values));
    }

    /**
     * Reverses the facet-id-to-field mapping so a field path from the URL can be resolved
     * back to the facet id the storefront filter panel uses.
     *
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    private function buildFieldToIdMap(Criteria $criteria): array
    {
        $mapping = $criteria->getExtension('nostoFilterMapping');
        if (!$mapping instanceof IdToFieldMapping) {
            return [];
        }

        return array_flip($mapping->getMap());
    }
```

`IdToFieldMapping` is already imported in `FilterHandler.php`.

## Follow-ups (not in this plan)

1. **`nosto/php-sdk`: inclusive range bounds.** `SearchOperation::addRangeFilter()` emits only `gt`/`lt`; the API accepts `gte`/`lte`. Until the SDK exposes them, `10~20` (inclusive per Nosto's contract) is sent as exclusive. Affects the pre-existing range-slider path identically. Raise against the SDK repo.
2. **Pinning facet groups in the request.** The plugin never passes a `facets:` input argument (`vendor/nosto/php-sdk/src/Operation/Search/SearchOperation.php:342` only *selects* the facets output field), so it depends entirely on Nosto's dynamic facet selection, capped at 15 groups. When the relevant facet is not returned, Task 8's reverse lookup finds no id and the filter applies without a selected-state checkbox. Passing known facet ids explicitly would make this deterministic.
3. **Sidebar selected state — and the filter being dropped on first interaction.** A shopper landing on a
   `products.filter.*` URL gets correctly filtered products but an unchecked filter panel and no removal
   chip. Worse, `listing.plugin.js:185-215` (`_buildRequest`) rebuilds the query string **solely** from the
   registered filter plugins' values, so the shopper's first interaction with any filter, sort, or page
   control silently drops the `products.filter.*` parameter and the filter disappears.

   **Recommended fix: a canonicalising redirect.** Redirect a field-path URL to the equivalent
   `?<facet-id>=<value>` URL (301/302) when the facet id is resolvable. That fixes all three symptoms at
   once — the browser URL then carries the parameter the JS actually reads, so the panel shows the
   selection, the removal chip works, and `_buildRequest` preserves it. Server-side rendering of the
   `selected` flag Nosto already returns per facet value
   (`src/Search/Response/GraphQL/Filter/Values/FilterValue.php:18`, populated at `Filter.php:85`,
   consumed by no template) would fix only the checkbox, not the drop-on-interaction.

   Note this is not a regression: before this change the parameter never applied at all. Afterwards it
   applies on landing and is lost on interaction — better, but inconsistent, which is why it is worth
   closing properly. See the Task 8 finding above for the full evidence.
4. **A filter matching nothing returns MORE products than no filter, via the fallback.** With
   `enableFallbackMechanism` on (default for the test channel), a zero-result Nosto response falls back
   to Shopware's own search, which knows nothing about `products.filter.*`. Measured live:
   `?search=main` → 3, `&products.filter.zzz=1` → **4**. This affects any filter that matches nothing,
   including a legitimate facet-id filter, so it is pre-existing fallback design rather than something
   this change introduced — but this change makes it reachable from an autocomplete link, and 4 > 3 is
   the same "filter looks ignored" symptom the ticket exists to remove.

   Note the field-path *validation* added here cannot fix this: it rejects malformed names
   (control characters, over-length, quotes) but `zzz` is a syntactically valid field name. Only Nosto
   can say whether a field exists, and gating on the fields present in the response would reintroduce
   the original bug, because Nosto returns at most 15 dynamically-selected facet groups and a valid
   keyword-facet field may legitimately be absent. The real fix is to suppress the zero-result fallback
   while a shopper filter is active — an empty filtered SERP is the honest answer. Out of scope here
   because it changes fallback semantics for all filters.

5. **End-to-end test with a real keyword facet.** Requires facets configured on the `shopware67` Nosto account plus search templates deployed without a `serpUrlMapping` override. Nosto-side setup; not needed to verify this fix.

## Task 11 (added 2026-08-10): canonicalise field-path filters to facet-id URLs — DONE

Closes the gap Task 8 could not. Instead of trying to fake selected state server-side, resolve the field
path to its Nosto facet id and **302-redirect** to the canonical URL, so the browser genuinely carries the
parameter the panel JS reads.

`src/Search/Request/Handler/CanonicalFilterUrlBuilder.php` (pure, 11 unit tests) plus wiring in
`AbstractRequestHandler::fetchResults()` after the existing merchant-redirect check, so merchant redirect
rules keep priority. `Redirect` gained an opt-in `permanent` flag defaulting to true: canonicalisation uses
**302**, because a facet id changes when a merchant recreates a facet and a cached 301 would pin a stale id.

Canonical forms emitted (matching what the panel expects):
- value → `?<facetId>=<v1>|<v2>` (single pipe — Nosto's field-path form uses a double pipe)
- range → `?min-<facetId>=<lower>&max-<facetId>=<upper>`, absent bounds omitted

Proven against the ticket's own example, using the real facet id matratzen-concord hardcodes:

```
IN : /search?search=viscoschaum&products.filter.skus.customFields.größe=140x200cm
OUT: /search?search=viscoschaum&68836248ec4277760d058e18=140x200cm
```

That output is byte-for-byte the URL that merchant produces via their hand-maintained `serpUrlMapping`, and
which was measured live returning 9 filtered results vs 19 unfiltered. **This removes the need for merchants
to maintain `serpUrlMapping` at all** — the plugin derives it from the Nosto response.

Other query parameters are preserved verbatim and in order (`order`, `p`, `search`). Loop safety is
covered: feeding the output back in returns null.

**Limits, deliberate:**
- Only `/search` canonicalises — `SearchController` is the sole consumer of `nostoRedirect`; the
  category/navigation path has no redirect consumer, so category pages keep applying filters directly
  (they filter correctly, but without panel state).
- Canonicalisation needs `nostoFilterMapping`, which `handleFiltersAndMapping()` only populates for a
  non-empty product result, so a zero-result filtered search does not canonicalise.
- A field absent from Nosto's returned facets (max 15 dynamic groups) is preserved verbatim and still
  applied directly — deliberately not dropped.
